answers.quote: Biodiversity is the term popularised by the sociobiologist Edward Wilson to describe the combined diversity at all the levels of biological organisation.
answers.notes: c01: term popularised by sociobiologist Edward Wilson.

answers.quote: The genetic variation shown by the medicinal plant Rauwolfia vomitoria growing in different Himalayan ranges might be in terms of the potency and concentration of the active chemical (reserpine) that the plant produces.
answers.notes: c03: Rauwolfia variation in reserpine potency/concentration = genetic diversity.

answers.quote: India has more than 50,000 genetically different strains of rice, and 1,000 varieties of mango.
answers.notes: c04: more than 50,000 genetically different strains of rice.

answers.answer: পশ্চিমঘাটে উভচর প্রজাতির বৈচিত্র্য পূর্বঘাটের চেয়ে বেশি
answers.quote: The diversity at the species level, for example, the Western Ghats have a greater amphibian species diversity than the Eastern Ghats.
answers.notes: c05: Western Ghats greater amphibian species diversity than Eastern Ghats.

answers.quote: At the ecosystem level, India, for instance, with its deserts, rain forests, mangroves, coral reefs, wetlands, estuaries, and alpine meadows has a greater ecosystem diversity than a Scandinavian country like Norway.
answers.notes: Stmt 1 false per c02 (diversity at all levels, not species level only); stmt 2 true per c06.

answers.quote: there are more than 20,000 species of ants, 3,00,000 species of beetles, 28,000 species of fishes and nearly 20,000 species of orchids.
answers.notes: c51: 3,00,000 species of beetles.

answers.quote: The genetic variation shown by the medicinal plant Rauwolfia vomitoria growing in different Himalayan ranges might be in terms of the potency and concentration of the active chemical (reserpine) that the plant produces.
answers.notes: Genetic=Rauwolfia (c03); species=Western/Eastern Ghats amphibians (c05); ecosystem=deserts/mangroves/wetlands etc. (c06).

answers.quote: According to the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN) (2004), the total number of plant and animal species described so far is slightly more than 1.5 million
answers.notes: c07: IUCN (2004) described slightly more than 1.5 million species.

answers.quote: Although India has only 2.4 per cent of the world's land area, its share of the global species diversity is an impressive 8.1 per cent. That is what makes our country one of the 12 mega diversity countries of the world.
answers.notes: c12: India has only 2.4 per cent of the world's land area.

answers.quote: Among animals, insects are the most speciesrich taxonomic group, making up more than 70 per cent of the total.
answers.notes: c10: insects most species-rich, more than 70 per cent of the total.

answers.quote: a more conservative and scientifically sound estimate made by Robert May places the global species diversity at about 7 million.
answers.notes: c08: Robert May's estimate places global diversity at about 7 million.

answers.answer: মাছ, উভচর, সরীসৃপ ও স্তন্যপায়ীর সম্মিলিত সংখ্যার চেয়ে বেশি
answers.quote: The number of fungi species in the world is more than the combined total of the species of fishes, amphibians, reptiles and mammals.
answers.notes: c11: fungi more than combined fishes, amphibians, reptiles and mammals.

answers.quote: If we accept May's global estimates, only 22 per cent of the total species have been recorded so far. Applying this proportion to India's diversity figures, we estimate that there are probably more than 1,00,000 plant species and more than 3,00,000 animal species yet to be discovered and described.
answers.notes: c14: probably more than 1,00,000 plant species yet to be discovered (3,00,000 figure is for animals).

answers.quote: Although India has only 2.4 per cent of the world's land area, its share of the global species diversity is an impressive 8.1 per cent. That is what makes our country one of the 12 mega diversity countries of the world.
answers.notes: Stmt 1 per c12 (one of 12 mega diversity countries); stmt 2 per c13 (45,000 plants, twice as many animals).

answers.quote: In general, species diversity decreases as we move away from the equator towards the poles.
answers.notes: c15: diversity decreases from equator towards poles.

answers.quote: Colombia located near the equator has nearly 1,400 species of birds while New York at 41° N has 105 species and Greenland at 71° N only 56 species. India, with much of its land area in the tropical latitudes, has more than 1,200 species of birds.
answers.notes: c16: Colombia near equator has nearly 1,400 bird species.

answers.quote: it is home to more than 40,000 species of plants, 3,000 of fishes, 1,300 of birds, 427 of mammals, 427 of amphibians, 378 of reptiles and of more than 1,25,000 invertebrates.
answers.notes: c17 documents the Amazon's exceptional richness (40,000 plants, 1,25,000+ invertebrates etc.); the superlative 'greatest' is not verbatim in the claims, but no other option has any claim support.

answers.quote: the great German naturalist and geographer Alexander von Humboldt observed that within a region species richness increased with increasing explored area, but only up to a limit. On a logarithmic scale, the relationship is a straight line described by the equation log S = log C + Z log A
answers.notes: c19: Alexander von Humboldt observed the species-area relationship.

answers.quote: Ecologists have discovered that the value of Z lies in the range of 0.1 to 0.2, if you analyse the speciesarea relationships among very large areas like the entire continents, you will find that the slope of the line to be much steeper (Z values in the range of 0.6 to 1.2). For example, for frugivorous (fruiteating) birds and mammals in the tropical forests of different continents, the slope is found to be 1.15.
answers.notes: c20: for very large areas like entire continents Z is 0.6 to 1.2 (0.1-0.2 is the general range).

answers.answer: ক্রান্তীয় অঞ্চলে মানুষের জনঘনত্ব সবচেয়ে বেশি
answers.quote: tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years and thus, had a long evolutionary time for species diversification, (b) Tropical environments, unlike temperate ones, are less seasonal, relatively more constant and predictable. Such constant environments promote niche specialisation and lead to a greater species diversity and (c) There is more solar energy available in the tropics, which contributes to higher productivity
answers.notes: c18 gives exactly three reasons (undisturbed time, constant predictable environment, more solar energy); human population density is not among them.

answers.answer: A ও R উভয়ই সঠিক এবং R, A-এর সঠিক ব্যাখ্যা
answers.quote: tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years and thus, had a long evolutionary time for species diversification, (b) Tropical environments, unlike temperate ones, are less seasonal, relatively more constant and predictable. Such constant environments promote niche specialisation and lead to a greater species diversity and (c) There is more solar energy available in the tropics, which contributes to higher productivity
answers.notes: c18(b): constant, predictable tropical environments promote niche specialisation - a stated cause of greater tropical diversity, so R correctly explains A.

answers.answer: তিনটি — সংকীর্ণ উপযোগিতা, ব্যাপক উপযোগিতা ও নৈতিক
answers.quote: They can be grouped into three categories: narrowly utilitarian, broadly utilitarian, and ethical.
answers.notes: c24: three categories - narrowly utilitarian, broadly utilitarian, ethical.

answers.quote: More than 25 per cent of the drugs currently sold in the market worldwide are derived from plants and 25,000 species of plants contribute to the traditional medicines used by native peoples around the world.
answers.notes: c25: more than 25 per cent of drugs sold worldwide are derived from plants.

answers.quote: we can develop a proper perspective through an analogy (the 'rivet popper hypothesis') used by Stanford ecologist Paul Ehrlich. Loss of rivets on the wings (key species that drive major ecosystem functions) is obviously a more serious threat to flight safety than loss of a few rivets on the seats or windows inside the plane.
answers.notes: c23: rivet popper hypothesis used by Stanford ecologist Paul Ehrlich.

answers.quote: The fast dwindling Amazon forest is estimated to produce, through photosynthesis, 20 per cent of the total oxygen in the earth's atmosphere. Pollination (without which plants cannot give us fruits or seeds) is another service, ecosystems provide through pollinators
answers.notes: c26: Amazon forest produces 20 per cent of total oxygen in earth's atmosphere.

answers.answer: বেশি প্রজাতির প্লটে মোট জীবভরের বছরে-বছরে ওঠানামা কম এবং উৎপাদনশীলতা বেশি
answers.quote: David Tilman's longterm ecosystem experiments using outdoor plots provide some tentative answers. Tilman found that plots with more species showed less yeartoyear variation in total biomass. He also showed that in his experiments, increased diversity contributed to higher productivity.
answers.notes: c22: Tilman - more species, less year-to-year variation in total biomass, higher productivity.

answers.answer: অর্থনৈতিক গুরুত্বের পণ্যের জন্য আণবিক, জিনগত ও প্রজাতি-স্তরের বৈচিত্র্য অন্বেষণ
answers.quote: With increasing resources put into 'bioprospecting' (exploring molecular, genetic and specieslevel diversity for products of economic importance), nations endowed with rich biodiversity can expect to reap enormous benefits.
answers.notes: c28: bioprospecting = exploring molecular, genetic and species-level diversity for products of economic importance.

answers.quote: The fast dwindling Amazon forest is estimated to produce, through photosynthesis, 20 per cent of the total oxygen in the earth's atmosphere. Pollination (without which plants cannot give us fruits or seeds) is another service, ecosystems provide through pollinators
answers.notes: Stmt 1: pollination is an ecosystem service (c26), i.e. broadly utilitarian (categories in c24). Stmt 2 false: intrinsic value is the ethical argument (c27), not narrowly utilitarian.

answers.quote: There are four major causes (' The Evil Quartet' is the sobriquet used to describe them). (i) Habitat loss and fragmentation: This is the most important cause driving animals and plants to extinction.
answers.notes: c33: habitat loss and fragmentation is the most important cause of extinction.

answers.quote: The IUCN Red List (2004) documents the extinction of 784 species (including 338 vertebrates, 359 invertebrates and 87 plants) in the last 500 years. Some examples of recent extinctions include the dodo (Mauritius), quagga (Africa), thylacine (Australia), Steller's Sea Cow (Russia) and three subspecies (Bali, Javan, Caspian) of tiger.
answers.notes: c29: dodo (Mauritius).

answers.quote: The Nile perch introduced into Lake Victoria in east Africa led eventually to the extinction of an ecologically unique assemblage of more than 200 species of cichlid fish in the lake.
answers.notes: c37: Nile perch led to extinction of more than 200 cichlid species in Lake Victoria.

answers.quote: You must be familiar with the environmental damage caused and threat posed to our native species by invasive weed species like carrot grass (Parthenium), Lantana and water hyacinth (Eicchornia). The recent illegal introduction of the African catfish Clarias gariepinus for aquaculture purposes is posing a threat to the indigenous catfishes in our rivers.
answers.notes: c38: illegally introduced African catfish Clarias gariepinus threatens indigenous catfishes.

answers.quote: when 'need' turns to 'greed', it leads to over -exploitation of natural resources. Many species extinctions in the last 500 years (Steller's sea cow, passenger pigeon) were due to overexploitation by humans.
answers.notes: c36: Steller's sea cow and passenger pigeon extinctions were due to overexploitation by humans.

answers.quote: During the long period (> 3 billion years) since the origin and diversification of life on earth there were five episodes of mass extinction of species. The difference is in the rates; the current species extinction rates are estimated to be 100 to 1,000 times faster than in the prehuman times and our activities are responsible for the faster rates.
answers.notes: c31: current extinction rates estimated 100 to 1,000 times faster than pre-human times.

answers.quote: more than 15,500 species worldwide are facing the threat of extinction. Presently, 12 per cent of all bird species, 23 per cent of all mammal species, 32 per cent of all amphibian species and 31per cent of all gymnosperm species in the world face the threat of extinction.
answers.notes: c30: 32 per cent of amphibian species face threat of extinction (12% birds, 23% mammals, 31% gymnosperms).

answers.quote: The IUCN Red List (2004) documents the extinction of 784 species (including 338 vertebrates, 359 invertebrates and 87 plants) in the last 500 years. Some examples of recent extinctions include the dodo (Mauritius), quagga (Africa), thylacine (Australia), Steller's Sea Cow (Russia) and three subspecies (Bali, Javan, Caspian) of tiger.
answers.notes: c29: dodo-Mauritius; quagga-Africa, thylacine-Australia, Steller's Sea Cow-Russia, so the other pairs are wrong.

answers.quote: Once covering more than 14 per cent of the earth's land surface, these rain forests now cover no more than 6 per cent. The Amazon rain forest (it is so huge that it is called the 'lungs of the planet') harbouring probably millions of species is being cut and cleared for cultivating soya beans or for conversion to grasslands for raising beef cattle.
answers.notes: Stmt 1 per c34 (rain forests 14% to no more than 6%); stmt 2 per c35 (large-territory mammals/birds and migratory animals badly affected by fragmentation).

answers.quote: When we conserve and protect the whole ecosystem, its biodiversity at all levels is protected - we save the entire forest to save the tiger. This approach is called in situ (on site) conservation.
answers.notes: c40: save the entire forest to save the tiger = in situ (on site) conservation.

answers.quote: Three of these hotspots – Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma and Himalaya – cover our country's exceptionally high biodiversity regions.
answers.notes: c44: Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma and Himalaya.

answers.answer: এগুলি বহু বিরল ও বিপন্ন উদ্ভিদের শেষ আশ্রয়
answers.quote: In Meghalaya, the sacred groves are the last refuges for a large number of rare and threatened plants.
answers.notes: c48: in Meghalaya sacred groves are last refuges for a large number of rare and threatened plants.

answers.quote: In India, ecologically unique and biodiversityrich regions are legally protected as biosphere reserves, national parks and sanctuaries. India now has 14 biosphere reserves, 90 national parks and 448 wildlife sanctuaries.
answers.notes: c46: 14 biosphere reserves, 90 national parks, 448 wildlife sanctuaries.

answers.quote: Zoological parks, botanical gardens and wildlife safari parks serve this purpose. Now gametes of threatened species can be preserved in viable and fertile condition for long periods using cryopreservation techniques, eggs can be fertilised in vitro, and plants can be propagated using tissue culture methods. Seeds of different genetic strains of commercially important plants can be kept for long periods in seed banks.
answers.notes: c49 lists ex situ methods (cryopreservation, in vitro, tissue culture, seed banks, zoos/gardens); a national park is in situ protection (c40/c46), not ex situ.

answers.quote: Zoological parks, botanical gardens and wildlife safari parks serve this purpose. Now gametes of threatened species can be preserved in viable and fertile condition for long periods using cryopreservation techniques, eggs can be fertilised in vitro, and plants can be propagated using tissue culture methods. Seeds of different genetic strains of commercially important plants can be kept for long periods in seed banks.
answers.notes: In situ: national park (c40/c46) and sacred grove (c47); ex situ: seed bank and zoological park (c49).

answers.quote: The historic Convention on Biological Diversity ('The Earth Summit') held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992, called upon all nations to take appropriate measures for conservation of biodiversity and sustainable utilisation of its benefits. In a followup, the World Summit on Sustainable Development held in 2002 in Johannesburg, South Africa, 190 countries pledged their commitment to achieve by 2010, a significant reduction in the current rate of biodiversity loss at global, regional and local levels.
answers.notes: c50: Earth Summit Rio 1992; Johannesburg 2002, 190 countries pledged significant reduction by 2010.
